housing: Rugby grew faster than anywhere else in the West Midlands between 2011 and 2021, with large new-build communities such as Houlton and Cawston. Older housing is concentrated in the Victorian terraces of New Bilton and around the town centre, where much of the private renting and a growing number of HMOs are found. Bilton, Hillmorton and Brownsover are mostly inter-war, post-war and 1970s–80s estates, and the rural villages have period cottages, some thatched.
checkinTips: New-build homes in Houlton and Cawston: photograph snagging marks, sealant, new turf and fences, parking spaces and any shared management areas.
Victorian terraces in New Bilton and near the centre: record damp at the base of walls, rear yards and alleys and where bins are kept.
Shared houses in the town: note the HMO licence number where needed and photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors and alarms.
Thatched and period cottages in Dunchurch and the villages: photograph thatch, chimneys, stoves and any oil tank with the fuel level.
Town-centre apartments: note fob and key counts, the intercom and allocated parking.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Rugby Borough Council's private sector housing team.
